newsitem.title: RWANDA: Heavy clashes on edge of Zairean city of Goma.
newsitem.headline: Heavy clashes on edge of Zairean city of Goma.

text.p: Tutsi fighters and Zairean soldiers exchanged mortar and machinegun fire on the edges of the eastern Zairean city of Goma on Thursday, sending thousands of refugees fleeing, aid workers and witnesses said.

"We have been seeing heavy fighting since 2.30 a.m. (00:30 GMT) with firing within Goma itself and outgoing and incoming mortar and heavy weapons fire about two km (one mile) north of Goma," said Reuters correspondent Christian Jennings.
He said mortar bombs exploded in Goma city in an area about two km (one mile) from the neighbouring Rwandan border town of Gisenyi and thousands of refugees were fleeing towards the border.

"There is fire from the Zairean army going north from the airport. We spoke this morning with a Zairean military official who said the rebels have broken through a line at Manigi, 10 km (six miles) outside of Goma," said Steve Pratt, an official with CARE International in the border city.
"The Zairean military official told us we should not worry because the Zaireans would leave the airport and let it be occupied by the other side," he added.
"Machinegun and rifle fire turned in the last three hours into mortars," said Michelle Quintaglie, spokeswoman for the World Food Programme in Goma. "The situation has deteriorated very rapidly."

"We are getting reports refugees in Kahindo camp, which is north of Goma and has 115,000 residents, are packing up and are on the move," said Quintaglie, adding Zaireans and Rwandan refugees fled towards Mugunga camp to the west of the city.
